what: OpenMM's dodecahedral solvation of 1L2Y, against the cubic one, and against the triclinic numerics in src/reference/triclinic.ts.
produced_by: tools/build_reference_system.py --pdb-id 1L2Y --box-shape dodecahedron --case 1L2Y-dodecahedron; facts pinned by test/triclinic-fixture.test.ts

savings.note: The water count falls by 25% where the volume falls by 29%: the solute is the same size in both, the padding is measured to the solute rather than between images, and whole molecules are kept or dropped. A ~22% atom saving is ~22% of a run's time and memory.

findings: Our boxVectorsForShape reproduces OpenMM's vectors exactly -- 0 difference, not merely close -- so both compute d/2 and d*sqrt(2)/2 from the same d.

Every edge of the cell (3.0796 nm) is longer than every perpendicular width (2.5145, 2.5145, 2.1776), so an edge-based cutoff bound would allow 1.5 nm where the real ceiling is 1.0888. That is the trap the bound exists for.

OpenMM's own default solvation fits the bound with 8.9% headroom. It is a live constraint, not a formality: the 1.2 nm cutoff some protocols use would not fit this box, so it has to be checked per system and reported.

still_refused_by.note: Every one of these calls rectangularBox, which throws. The reference four are the next stage and are testable in the no-GPU lane against OpenMM's energy for this fixture; PME's reciprocal lattice is the hard one.
